content:
Ratio and proportion is Class 6's most word-problem-heavy chapter — dividing amounts in a ratio, testing proportions and the unitary method. Here is what the IMO Class 6 chapter tests, the facts, and a free 10-question test.

What the Class 6 Maths Olympiad Ratio and Proportion chapter tests

  • Ratios in simplest form (same units!)
  • Dividing a quantity in a given ratio
  • Proportion: a : b :: c : d ⇔ ad = bc
  • The unitary method for cost, speed and work

Key facts your child should know

  • A ratio compares quantities in the SAME unit and has no units itself.
  • To divide ₹250 in the ratio 3 : 2 — 5 parts, one part 50, shares 150 and 100.
  • Product of extremes = product of means: 2 : 3 :: 8 : 12 since 2×12 = 3×8.
  • Unitary method: go DOWN to one unit, then UP to what is asked.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Comparing metres with centimetres without converting.
  • Splitting in a ratio without totalling the parts first.
  • Multiplying instead of dividing in the unitary step.

questions.q: Divide Rs 4500 in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. Find the largest share.
Find the mean proportional between 9 and 16.
If 12 identical machines produce 1800 items in 6 hours, how many items will 8 machines produce in 9 hours?
If the shadow of a 6 m pole is 4 m long, find the shadow of a 15 m tree at the same time.
If 40% of a number is equal to 2/3 of another number, find the ratio of the first to the second.
Divide 3600 into three parts such that the second is twice the first and the third is thrice the first.
A gear with 20 teeth meshes with one having 35 teeth. If the smaller gear makes 70 revolutions, how many does the larger make?
If a : b = 5 : 8, find (a + b) : (a - b) given a < b.
The ratio of speed of a cycle to a car is 2 : 5. If the car covers 100 km in 2 hours, find the cycle speed.
questions.explanation: Car speed = 50 km/h. Cycle = 2/5 x 50 = 20 km/h.

faq.q: How do you divide ₹250 in the ratio 3 : 2?
faq.a: Total parts = 5, one part = ₹50, so the shares are ₹150 and ₹100.

faq.q: How do you check if four numbers are in proportion?
faq.a: Multiply the extremes and the means — 2, 3, 8, 12 are in proportion because 2 × 12 = 3 × 8 = 24.
